background_notes.justification: The unit balls centered at points of K cover K, hence finitely many suffice by compactness. The triangle inequality bounds the norm of every covered point by 1 plus the maximum norm of the finitely many centers (including 0 in this maximum handles an empty family). Each absolute coordinate is at most the Euclidean norm, so increasing the finite bound to a positive b gives the coordinate box. In R^0 the coordinate conditions are vacuous.

background_notes.fact: For b>0, n>0 and 0<h<=1, the box [-b,b]^n has a finite cover by at most (2b+2)^n h^(-n) coordinate boxes, each of Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies the positive box bound.

background_notes.justification: Put k=ceil(2b/h), a positive integer, and split each interval into k equal closed subintervals of length 2b/k<=h. There are k^n product boxes. The ceiling bound gives k<=2b/h+1<=(2b+1)/h<=(2b+2)/h. For two points in a box each coordinate difference has absolute value at most h, so their squared Euclidean distance is at most n h^2. Thus the asserted diameter bound holds. Calling these boxes cubes does not affect either estimate.

background_notes.fact: For fixed positive finite K and p, K h^p tends to zero as h tends to zero through positive values. For n>0 and a>n, the displayed cover costs C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a equal C n^(a/2)h^(a-n); the associated diameter bound sqrt(n)h also tends to zero.
